newsitem.title: USA: Ahmanson ends effort to acquire Great Western.
newsitem.headline: Ahmanson ends effort to acquire Great Western.

text.p: H.F. Ahmanson & Co. said on Wednesday it withdrew its $6.73 billion bid to acquire Great Western Financial Corp., saying it was terminating all pending litigation related to the proposal.

Ahmanson issued its announcement a day after the Delaware Chancery Court ruled that Great Western could hold its special shareholders meeting on June 13 to vote on its planned $6.74 billion merger with Seattle-based Washington Mutual Inc.
The ruling left Ahmanson few options but to raise its bid, which would dilute its stock and leave the banking company open to criticism from its own stockholders.
Ahmanson, the Irwindale, Calif.-based parent of Home Savings of America, launched its hostile takeover offer for Great Western in February.
Ahmanson, a $48 billion-asset company, is the parent of Home Savings of America, one of the largest U.S. thrifts.

Chatsworth, Calif.-based Great Western sought a white knight and subsequently agreed to be acquired by Washington Mutual in a deal that will create the largest U.S. thrift, with $86 billion in assets.
In a statement issued early Wednesday, Ahmanson Chairman and Chief Executive Charles Rinehart said the company concluded it could not win without raising its bid but decided against doing so.

For three months, Ahmanson and Washington Mutual waged a war of words over who had the superior offer, appealing to Great Western shareholders in full-page advertisements in major newspapers. Ahmanson argued that because both it and Great Western were located in the same geographic area, it could wring more expense reductions from a combination.
Washington Mutual cited its record of more than 20 successful acquisitions and said it could cut expenses and grow revenue at the same time.

"We remain absolutely committed to shareholder value and will continue to exercise discipline in merger efforts as in all other endeavours," Rinehart said. "We still believe that Great Western was an attractive partner, but not at the expense of returns to our shareholders."

Rinehart said Ahmanson will aggressively pursue its strategy to grow as a full-service bank for consumers and small business. He said the company will seek to improve asset quality, become more efficient and capitalise on a strong market position, while continuing its capital management and stock buyback programmes.
